R5D-bear-atv-0004.name: 830 m E of 3 Mile Creek
R5D-bear-atv-0004.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).
R5D-bear-atv-0004.parkWhat: where the truck road ends (Cp153-1-Br1); unload the ATV (all terrain vehicle)

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2019 (7 years old), 170 m NW: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
Burn from 2017 (fire C30892), 460 m NW: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
S facing slope, 20 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from Soda Creek, about 51 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate). Via Soda Creek Townsite Rd, Hwy 97, Beaver Lake Rd, Likely Rd.
Park: 52.52032, -121.78716, where the truck road ends (Cp153-1-Br1); unload the ATV (all terrain vehicle). Map links below.
Ride: 2.8 km on Cp153-1-Br1, Cp397-5-Sp1 by ATV (all terrain vehicle) or 4x4 on rough road, estimate. Then walk 90 m E, climb about 31 m.

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 5-2, Region 5. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-07, closures 2026-10-16.
